transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-16 15:00 UTC | Duration: 62m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Sara Lopez (Meridian CTO), Daniel Cho (ML Eng), Priya Nair (Product), Alex Reed (Security), Lina Gomez (SRE)

Summary (auto-gen): quick scoping for model selection and POC path. Focus on open models, 32k-64k context, multilingual capability, and how tool-calling will be handled across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

00:00:05 Jamie (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
00:00:12 Sara (Meridian): hey Sara here, CTO, we've got Daniel, Priya, Alex and Lina.
00:00:18 Jamie: perfect. i'm jamie from Redwood, ravi's on to dig into the technicals.
00:00:24 Ravi (SE): hi all, yep, happy to jump into latency and batching.
00:00:33 Priya: our goal today is to understand model options for a conversational assistant that also calls our search and billing tools, also needs good multi language support.
00:00:42 Daniel: couple constraints: some conversations will reference long docs, up to 100k characters, so context length matters. also we prefer open models for cost and licensing.
00:00:55 Ravi: mm-hm, so when you say 100k chars, that's roughly 20-40k tokens depending, so are you thinking 32k or 64k windows?
00:01:05 Daniel: ideally 64k in the long term. but most interactions will be 8-16k tokens, occasional long threads hit higher.
00:01:15 Alex (Security): and from security side, we need either Redwood Dedicated with private networking or a Private on-prem option—no PII leaving our VPC for pilot. also KMS integration and audit logs retention for 12 months.
00:01:29 Jamie: noted. Redwood supports SSO/SAML, KMS integrations, and audit logs; for PII we typically recommend Private if you need complete control.
00:01:40 Lina (SRE): curious on the perf hit for 64k context. how much does quantization or KV cache help?
00:01:49 Ravi: good q. for most open models, 64k is heavier but we've got continuous KV cache and chunked attention optimizations in our runtime. quantized weights (4-bit) reduce memory but can add some latency depending on the kernel path. we can produce a baseline comparing 16k vs 32k vs 64k on Mistral/Falcon variants.
00:02:10 Sara: can you talk through concrete model candidates and tradeoffs? we want multilingual out of box — spanish, portuguese, french, hindi, japanese.
00:02:18 Jamie: sure. high-level candidates: Mistral Instruct-style variants (good cost/quality for instruction), Falcon-40B for long-context variants (some community forks add 32k/64k), RedPajama or Llama 2 derivatives for controllable cost and ecosystem. there are also multilingual-focused models like M2M or some NLLB-based hybrids, but usually you combine a strong base model with translation or multilingual fine-tuning.
00:02:45 Daniel: we've tried an off-the-shelf Llama 2 - it struggled on Hindi and some technical Portuguese. are there recommended approach — translation pre-processing or a multilingual model?
00:02:56 Ravi: both are valid. translation pre/post processing gives consistent behavior but adds latency and costs. a multilingual model with fine-tuning on your domain might be better long term. we typically suggest an A/B between a multilingual base and a translation pipeline during POC.
00:03:13 Priya: about tool-calling: we need to call our search microservice, a knowledge connector to vector DB, and a billing API to fetch subscriptions. do you support function calling or structured responses?
00:03:25 Jamie: yes — our API supports structured tool-calling, function calls, and we can integrate with your external tools using a secure service account. we can also enforce sanitization and response schema to avoid leaking calls.
00:03:37 Ravi: technical addendum: for retrieval-augmented generation we recommend embeddings + hybrid search. caching frequently used docs (prefix caching) reduces token usage for repeated queries.
00:03:47 Alex: any concerns about calling external tools from Hosted? we worried about egress and logs.
00:03:53 Jamie: Hosted can call external endpoints but for sensitive data we'd steer customers to Dedicated with private networking or Private. Hosted has SOC2 and encryption at rest, but you retain control best with Private for PII-in-VPC.
00:04:10 Lina: performance SLOs for Dedicated vs Hosted? we need <200ms generator latency on short prompts, and under-1s for typical Q/A chains.
00:04:20 Ravi: short prompts in hosted environment with smaller models will hit 50-200ms for token generation depending on model size. for 1s Q/A chains that's pretty achievable with Dedicated reserved GPU pools—we can configure autoscaling and burst lanes. we'll share a matrix of observed p99 latencies across candidate models.
00:04:44 Daniel: curious about cost for 64k context runs, token count skyrockets — what levers do we have?
00:04:52 Ravi: levers: prefix/KV caching, chunked retrieval (summarize long docs into condensed context), quantization for cheaper GPUs, and routing to smaller models for meta tasks. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and quant profiles for your workload.
00:05:09 Priya: what about fine-tuning vs instruction tuning vs retrieval?
00:05:13 Jamie: retrieval-first is usually faster to iterate; instruction tuning or SFT is heavier but gives more consistent outputs for critical flows. many customers combine retrieval for facts and a small tuned model for task handling.
00:05:25 Sara: do you support multilingual embeddings or do we need language-specific indexes?
00:05:30 Ravi: our embedding catalog includes multilingual models; we also recommend language-agnostic embeddings like LaBSE or multilingual variants for a single index, but for precision you can use language-specific indexes. depends on your retrieval requirements.
00:05:45 Alex: security checklist — do you offer customer-managed keys (CMK) with HSM?
00:05:50 Jamie: yes, we support KMS integrations and for Private on-prem we can integrate with customer HSMs. we'll share the security pack.
00:05:58 Daniel: let's talk about evaluation — what should we send for your baselines?
00:06:03 Ravi: best is a redacted sample of 100-200 representative conversations, some long docs, and especially the multilingual edge cases. also a few prompt templates and the expected output schema for tool-calls. we'll run latency and quality checks against candidate models.
00:06:19 Priya: how long for a POC?
00:06:22 Jamie: typical POC is 3-6 weeks — week 1: data share and baseline, weeks 2-3: tuning and benchmarks, week 4+: pilot in Dedicated or Private depending. we can compress timeline if Meridian provides data quickly.
00:06:34 Lina: any caveats about on-prem deployment resource needs? GPUs, networking, ops?
00:06:39 Ravi: on-prem needs depend on model choice and concurrency. a 32k token model needs more GPU memory and NVLink-friendly setup. we'll propose an ops footprint for two scenarios: low-concurrency high-context (batchy) and real-time low-latency.
00:06:55 Sara: what about vendor lock-in — how portable are models and pipelines?
00:06:59 Jamie: we avoid lock-in: models are standard open checkpoints, runtime configs are portable, and we provide exportable embeddings and trace logs. Dedicated and Private let you keep control of artifacts.
00:07:12 Daniel: any recommended starting combo for our use case?
00:07:16 Ravi: quick recommendation: start with a multilingual-capable Mistral or Llama-variant for day-to-day (16k window) and run Falcon-40B-extended or community 64k forks for long-document flows. use retrieval and translation A/B for non-Latin scripts.
00:07:31 Priya: ok, that feels actionable.
00:07:35 Jamie: recap: we'll send model/cost/latency matrix, security pack, and Ravi will run baselines on two candidate models with 16k/32k/64k. Meridian provides sample data and multilingual cases. schedule on-prem deep dive after Alex shares security must-haves.
00:07:53 Alex: noted. one more: audit log retention APIs — can we query logs programmatically?
00:07:59 Jamie: yes, audit export APIs available on Dedicated/Private, and hosted has admin UI exports.
00:08:06 Sara: great — thanks everyone. any final q's?
00:08:10 Daniel: none from me.
00:08:12 Priya: all good.
00:08:15 Jamie: thanks all — we'll follow up with the decks and the matrix.
00:08:19 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: minor mis-heard words (K-V cash vs KV cache), speaker attribution was automated — Ravi occasionally shows as Speaker 2 in system, manual notes corrected above.
